historical_claims.anchor: Tambudzai, called Tambu, is telling us how she grew up in Rhodesia
Then Nhamo becomes ill and dies.
Babamukuru decides that the family has another moral problem
Tambu is eventually allowed to attend.
One evening Nyasha suffers a severe breakdown.

editorial_scope: Plot narrated from Tambu’s perspective; does not equate colonial social violence with a clinical diagnosis of Nyasha.

work.note: Existing survey chapter label '1988 · Nervous Conditions' supplies the work's publication year; bibliography identifies the work. This dates publication, not its fictional setting or the lecture's creation.

description: Follows Tambu’s education and family, examining colonial institutions, gender, class, bodily distress, and the cost of an imagined future. Covers An unexpected beginning; Babamukuru's house; Nyasha's struggle at home; Where Tambu leaves us.
